name: Christina Bohannan
page_title: Christina Bohannan's Issue Positions (Political Courage Test)
on_the_ballot: Running, Democratic for U.S. House (IA) - District 1

positions.question: Do you support the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade?

evidence.text: "49 years ago today, #SCOTUS ruled in favor of women in Roe v Wade. But the battle over women’s reproductive freedom continues. The radical right is working to restrict access to safe abortions. We need leaders who fight for women, not against them."
"Codify Roe. Respect our freedoms. It’s time for real representation."

"Today marks the 51st anniversary of Roe v Wade. Let’s understand where @millermeeks wants to take us: back. Back to when women had no agency, no freedom to control their bodies, no way to get safe and necessary reproductive care. We will not go back. #RoeVWade"
Voted against HJR 5 "Amends the State Constitution to Repeal the Right to an Abortion"

positions.question: Do you support expanding federal funding to support social safety net programs such as Social Security and Medicare?

evidence.text: "After some events in Davenport, my team stopped by Wendy’s for Frosties. And I spent a few more minutes talking with one more voter about the importance of protecting Social Security."

"Even though we have nursing shortages in Iowa, and rural hospitals are closing, and some in Southeast Iowa have to drive 90 minutes to see a doctor, @RepMMM Miller-Meeks voted this week to allow massive and immediate cuts to Medicare."
"We also talked about Medicare, and about how hard it is for small-town hospitals to retain doctors. Iowans deserve quality, accessible health care--and I will work hard to be sure we get it."

"When @RepMMM voted to shut down the gov't this week, she voted against social security, Medicare, and veterans benefits. And she voted against families getting that last child tax credit payment before the holidays."

evidence.text: "Now our military members are not getting paid. @millermeeks if you care about Iowa’s service members, tell McCarthy to pass the bipartisan senate CR NOW."

positions.question: Do you support federal spending as a means of promoting economic growth (e.g. grants, tax incentives)?

evidence.text: "As reported this a.m. by @KCRG, Iowa leads the nation for structurally deficient bridges. ( I have something to say about that: #infrastructure = safety = economy"
"Iowa deserves a Congresswoman who will say YES to the infrastructure that will improve our state, our communities, our economy. @RepMMM said no."

"Iowa's bridges and roads are crumbling; our internet access and speed are some of the worst in the country. The bipartisan #Infrastructure plan will benefit Iowa as much as or more than any other state in the country. And @RepMMM voted against it."

"When running for Congress, @RepMM told Iowans her top priority would be an infrastructure bill, saying "we really need [it]." But this week she voted the way her party bosses told her to and opposed critical infrastructure investments for Iowa."

positions.question: Do you support the federal government increasing funding for affordable housing programs?

evidence.text: "Yesterday I had a great conversation with voters at the Coal Palace Cafe in Ottumwa. We talked affordable housing, childcare, and the local city council race. Onward in Wapello County!"

positions.question: Do you support the federal government taking action, beyond those of the Federal Reserve, to alleviate inflation?

evidence.text: "2/2 CHIPS will fix our supply chain on thousands of products, reduce inflation, protect national security, & create good manufacturing jobs in states like Iowa. There's no good reason for @RepMMM's vote: she's obeying her party bosses instead of doing what Iowans need her to do."

"Yesterday during my stop in Jasper County, we talked about the wind blade manufacturing plant reopening. It's huge for Newton, and it is happening thanks to the Inflation Reduction Act, which my opponent voted against."

positions.question: Do you support the forgiveness of federal student loan debt?

positions.question: Should the government be able to regulate the cost of prescription drugs?

evidence.text: "If Miller-Meeks fought 1/10 as hard for her constituents who need prescription drugs as she does for drug company profits, I would drop out of this race today. #IA01"

"Last year @millermeeks sided with Big Pharma companies—voting against legislation to cap the price of insulin & lower drug prices. Now MM is siding with her special interest friends on Wall Street by trying to gut protections for Iowa families’ retirements. Shameful."
Voted in favor of HF 263 "Limits the Out of Pocket Cost for an Insulin Prescription at $100"

"Amazing that you continue to be so outspoken against lowering drug prices. To heck with regular Iowans who rely on things like insulin to stay alive, right? I guess it’s hard to pay attention to your constituents when the Pharma "industry" gave you a hefty donation this year."
